thread:
Maya S: Hey team — customer reported that after we rotated their API key last night they can still make requests with the old key from some of their edge hosts. We've rotated in Vault and updated DB, but about ~20% of requests still succeed with the revoked key. Not sure where the old secret is being accepted. Any ideas?

Jamal R: That sounds like either a validation cache or we have multiple auth services and one hasn't picked up the new revocation. Which path are those requests hitting? gateway -> auth -> runtime?

Maya S: It's the usual path: infra-proxy (envoy) -> authsvc (k8s service) -> runtime. Customer sent curl output showing 200 for old key from some IPs and 401 from others. They also said restarting their app pod briefly fixed it for that pod. :confused:

Alex W: Interesting. If a restart fixes it, suggests the secret was read into process memory / sidecar cache. Do we have any in-memory caching in authsvc or the envoy sidecar that stores validated API keys?

Tara Ops: We have a sidecar library (redwood-auth-proxy) that caches validated tokens for 5m to avoid roundtrips to Vault on every request. There's also a short-lived local auth cache in authsvc itself (LRU). Both are TTL-based. Vault rotation propagation for us should be immediate because we pull from Vault on validation, but if clients are using cached validation results we could see this.

Maya S: Customer says some requests go through via edge-hosted CDN/proxy. Could CDN be caching Authorization headers? They claim they pass Authorization in header — CDNs normally don't cache based on auth but some misconfig could.

Jamal R: Can you ask for a failing and succeeding request pair and full raw headers? If envoy is caching or the edge is reusing an old connection with an old header, that shouldn't matter. But the restart hint points to local cache. Also, did we revoke the key in both Vault and our auth DB? Sometimes rotation flow forgets to mark key revoked in internal auth index.

Maya S: I checked Vault and our auth_keys table has the new key and old key status=revoked. Revocation event sent to webhook; webhook returned 200. Here's the customer's minimal repro:

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer OLDKEY" \ 
  https://api.customer.example/v1/endpoint

# response: 200 OK (from some edge host)
```

Jamal R: Can you run this against our internal authsvc directly to emulate validation path? E.g. `curl -X POST http://authsvc.internal/validate -d '{"key":"OLDKEY"}'` and paste response. If authsvc returns OK but Vault shows revoked, something is wrong with our lookup cache.

Alex W: Also check the sidecar version on their hosts. We patched the cache invalidation in redwood-auth-proxy last quarter; older versions won't get the revocation pubsub. If their edge hosts haven't rolled, they may keep allowing old keys until TTL expiry.

Maya S: Got direct authsvc check back from customer: authsvc.validate returned 200 for OLDKEY from the affected host. From our cluster, hitting same authsvc pod returns 401. So authsvc instance on their cluster is returning OK while ours is enforcing revocation.

Tara Ops: That implies either their authsvc uses a local persistent cache file, or they're pinned to an older sidecar binary that doesn't subscribe to the revocation topic. Do we have the agent that pushes revocation notifications? Vault -> events -> revocation-topic -> sidecars/subscribers. VaultBot should show an event.

VaultBot: Revocation event published to topic revocations at 2026-11-02T03:12:05Z for key id kd_82b4. Webhook fanout status: 5 subs, 5 acks, 0 failures.

Maya S: Webhook fanout shows acked. Customer's cluster won't be one of our subs for dedicated private customers. They run our on-prem package; sidecars subscribe to revocation topic via NATS we provision. They reported using our v1.3 installer. I think v1.3 sidecar didn't auto-subscribe — it relied on poll-based fallback with a 10m poll interval. That would explain why some hosts still accepted old key.

Jamal R: That matches. Polling interval 10m means old keys can be accepted until poll. Restart forcing immediate poll would explain restart fix. Customer restart fixed pod temporarily.

Alex W: Short-term mitigation: ask customer to restart the auth proxy sidecar on affected pods or increase poll frequency. Long-term: we should backport a hotfix to the v1.3 sidecar to reduce poll TTL and emit a post-rotation webhook to the local agent to flush caches. Also document post-rotation checklist for on-prem customers.

Maya S: I pushed these steps to the customer: 1) Restart redwood-auth-proxy on affected hosts (systemctl restart r-auth or kubectl rollout restart daemonset) 2) Confirm authsvc.validate returns 401 for OLDKEY 3) If they can't restart, reduce poll interval in /etc/redwood/agent.conf to 30s and reload agent. They tried restart and immediately saw 401 for old key, good.

Tara Ops: I'll open an eng-infra ticket to backport cache invalidation + add post-rotation hook to our release train. We should also add a check in rotation playbook to verify revocation across on-prem subscribers.

Alex W: Also add an automated smoke test after rotation that attempts validation of the old key from multiple vantage points (edge, on-prem, internal) and fails the rotation if any accept it. That would have caught this.

Maya S: Customer happy for now, asked for a timeline on permanent fix. I've created a follow-up issue and attached logs. Will loop in eng-infra and on-call.

Jamal R: Thanks — summary: root cause = on-prem agent sidecar using poll-based revocation path with long TTL (v1.3). Fixes: restart/force-poll (customer immediate), change agent config or upgrade to v1.4, and platform change to push revocation webhook that triggers cache flush. Follow-ups: backport hotfix, add rotation smoke tests, update on-prem rotation docs.

Maya S: Added labels: urgent, customer-impacting. Pinged @Alex W for eng-infra triage. :thumbsup:

Alex W: I'll take the triage and add to next sprint; also will draft a quick KB article for on-prem rotation steps.

Maya S: Thanks team — closing thread once KB link is live and eng-infra confirms timeline.
